conclusion.label: rejects

report:
### Conclusion

The claim that having an abortion increases a woman's risk of breast cancer is false and refutes established scientific consensus. Leading global and national health organizations—including the National Cancer Institute (NCI), the American Cancer Society (ACS), the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), and the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine (NASEM)—unanimously agree that induced abortion is not associated with an increased risk of breast cancer.

Scientific research demonstrates that higher-quality, prospective cohort studies show no connection between abortion and breast cancer. Methodological errors in earlier, smaller studies—such as recall bias—erroneously suggested a link. Comprehensive reanalyses combining data across tens of thousands of women worldwide confirm that neither induced abortion nor miscarriage raises a woman's risk of developing pre- or postmenopausal breast cancer.

### Sources

* **American Cancer Society:** https://www.cancer.org/cancer/risk-prevention/medical-treatments/abortion-and-breast-cancer-risk.html
* **Susan G. Komen:** https://www.komen.org/breast-cancer/facts-statistics/research-studies/topics/abortion-and-breast-cancer-risk/
* **Breastcancer.org:** https://www.breastcancer.org/risk/risk-factors/abortion
* **National Academies / ACPeds summary:** https://acpeds.org/reproductive-choices-of-young-women-affecting-future-breast-cancer-risk/
